Aisha — quick read and recommendations below. High level: we should avoid a single aggregate cap that ties to total fees unless we get more favorable multiples or an explicit carve-out for security/data incidents. Suggested approach:

1) Anchor to usage bands (preferred): propose tiered caps tied to trailing 12-month fees — e.g., for Band A (>$500k ARR) cap = 1x trailing 12-month fees; Band B ($100k–$500k) cap = 2x trailing 12-month fees; Band C (<$100k) cap = 3x trailing 12-month fees. This gives commercial predictability and scales with usage.

2) Aggregate maximum (fallback): if they insist on contract-wide aggregate, propose cap = 2x total fees paid in the contract term (not unlimited), with an annualized deposit floor to limit exposure in early high-spend years.

3) Carve-outs: we preserve usual carve-outs for fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity, but push to limit consequential damages carve-out to third-party downstream claims only and exclude direct economic loss tied to SLA breaches.

4) IP & data breaches: retain separate indemnity for IP infringement and severe data breach; propose higher cap (e.g., 3x annual) in those narrow instances or unlimited for IP indemnity if we can get reciprocal indemnity from them.

I can draft redline text for both the MSA and the order form. If you want to be commercial, recommend the usage-band anchor plus an explicit maximum multiple for the term as our counter.

—Karthik

Samantha / Acme Legal — thanks for the redlines and patience while we coordinated internally. Attached is our proposed counter (summarized below) and a clean redline will follow from Karthik. Please review and let us know whether this is workable for you: 

Summary of Redwood counter (high-level):
- Primary proposal: usage-band anchored cap tied to trailing 12-month fees with clear bands (Band A/B/C); provides predictability as spend evolves.
- Fallback: if Acme requires a contract-wide aggregate cap, Redwood will accept an aggregate cap equal to 2x total fees paid in the contract term, subject to a 6-month milestone review (we can reset to annualized caps if usage stabilizes).
- Carve-outs: Redwood will preserve standard carve-outs for fraud, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and IP indemnity. Consequential damages carve-out will be narrowed to exclude direct economic loss from SLA breaches; consequential damages will otherwise remain excluded for indirect downstream claims.
- IP/Data: propose separate indemnity treatment; for IP claims we seek reciprocal indemnity and higher per-claim cap (3x annualized fees) or, if reciprocal language unacceptable, limited unlimited indemnity for IP only with additional underwriting.
